newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Overheated Russian MinFins track Brady market dip.
newsitem.headline: Overheated Russian MinFins track Brady market dip.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds fell in lively trading on Wednesday on profit-taking and following Vnesh debt selling on fears of a rise in U.S. interest rates, dealers said.

Traders on the Brady market were nervously awaiting next week's Federal Open Market Committee Meeting to see if and by how much the U.S. raises interest rates. Dealers are speculating on a rise of 25 basis points.
"MinFins are linked to these rates. They are going down, tracking Vnesh debt which started easing yesterday," Imperial Bank dealer Alexei Denisov said.
Dealers said profit-taking was another bearish factor on the market, overheated after the rise last week and on Monday.
"There has been a big rise and a dip is normal," an ICFI Moscow Partners bank dealer said, but added trading volumes were not high, and the market was going down without deals.
Dealers said concern about President Boris Yeltsin's heart surgery was also overshadowing the market.
They added the third, fourth and fifth tranches had support at 77.30-77.40, 51.10-51.15 and 33.10-33.15 respectively.
